::: {.lead}
Today you write the start of a formal letter and a CV, with an AI
assistant and Word, and you check what the AI wrote. Each experiment has
two parts. **Part A** is in the AI assistant and Word on the lab computer.
**Part B** is on a simulator of the interactive lesson: on paper, scan its
QR code; on the screen, click its link. After each step, write your result
in its box. At the end, copy your key results into the table.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a lab computer with Word, a browser and an AI assistant
  that the university allows (for example `copilot.microsoft.com`).
- **No lab computer today?** Do Part B of each experiment on your phone. Do
  Part A later on any computer with Word.
- **Never type personal data** (an ID number, your home address, a phone
  number) into an AI tool or a CV: use made-up details in this lecture.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive lesson, every step has a check that answers
  at once.

## Experiment 1 · The parts of a formal letter

**The idea:** a **formal letter** goes to a company, a school or an office.
Its parts, from the top: your address and the **date**; the reader's name
and address; the **subject line**; the **greeting** (*Dear Mr Khalil,*);
three short paragraphs (why you write; about you; what you ask, and
thanks); the closing *Yours sincerely,* and your name. The tone is polite
and clear. An AI chat can draft the text; you check every fact and every
part.

**Aim:** let an AI draft a formal letter, and check it part by part.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the apps (an AI assistant and Word)**
:::

1. Send this prompt: *Write a formal letter to Mr Ahmad Khalil, Manager of
   the City Library. Our study group of 6 students asks to use the meeting
   room on Thursday 4 December, from 1 to 3 p.m. Three short paragraphs,
   formal tone.* Paste the letter into Word with **Keep Text Only**. Which
   parts of a formal letter are missing, or only a gap like *[Your
   Address]*?

   {{< record "Missing parts (or gaps): …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   An AI letter usually has the greeting (*Dear Mr Khalil,*), three
   paragraphs and the closing. Often **your address, the date or the
   subject line** are missing, or only gaps like *[Your Address]*: you
   add them with made-up details.
   :::

   ::: {.order}
   Put the parts of a formal letter in order, from the top.

   1. your address and the date
   2. the reader's name and address
   3. the subject line
   4. the greeting
   5. the three short paragraphs
   6. the closing and your name

   Why: A formal letter has fixed parts, from your address at the top to your name at the bottom.
   :::

2. Write a **subject line** above the greeting. Then check the facts of the
   letter: Thursday 4 December, 1 to 3 p.m., 6 students. Correct anything
   that is wrong, and save the file as `library-letter.docx`.

   {{< record "My subject line … ; a fact that I corrected (or: none)" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good subject line, for example **Subject: Request to use the meeting
   room on 4 December**. The facts must be the ones of your prompt; delete
   any promise or detail that the AI added.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which subject line fits the letter?

   - [x] Subject: Request to use the meeting room on 4 December

     Why: It says what the letter is about, in one line.

   - [ ] Subject: Hello!

     Why: A subject line gives the topic, not a greeting.

   - [ ] Subject: Letter

     Why: Every letter is a letter: say what this one is about.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-05/sims/letter-builder.html" poster="../../week-05/sims/letter-builder.png" title="Letter Builder: the parts of a formal letter" >}}

3. In **Letter Builder**, put Sami's letter together, part by part, from
   the top. Which part comes right after the date?

   {{< record "After the date comes …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **The address of the company**: the reader's name and address (Ms Rana
   Saleh, HR Manager, Sunrise Company). Then the subject line, the
   greeting, the three paragraphs, the closing and Sami's name.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   In Letter Builder, which part comes just before the greeting?

   - [x] the subject line

     Why: The reader sees the topic, then the greeting.

   - [ ] the closing

     Why: The closing comes at the end, before your name.

   - [ ] your address

     Why: Your address is at the very top.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · A one-page CV

**The idea:** a **CV** tells a company about you, on **one page**. Its parts:
contact details (name, e-mail, city; no ID number), a **profile** of 2–3
true sentences, education (the newest first, with the years), experience
(real jobs), skills and languages. Word has **CV templates** (File › New,
search "CV" or "resume"). AI can suggest good words for the profile: give it
your real facts, and keep only what is true.

**Aim:** start a CV from a template, and get a true profile from AI.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the apps (Word and an AI assistant)**
:::

1. In Word, click **File › New** and search for **CV** (or **resume**).
   Open a simple template. Write the names of its parts (its headings).

   {{< record "The parts of the template" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A simple template has parts like **contact details**, **profile** (or
   summary), **education**, **experience** and **skills**, sometimes
   **languages**. You type your facts in place of the example text.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Which details go into a CV? Sort them.

   Yes: they belong in a CV
   :   your name, e-mail and city

       Why: The contact details that a company needs.

   :   your education, the newest first

       Why: The reader sees your newest study first.

   :   your skills, like Word and Excel

       Why: Skills that you really have.

   No: never in a CV
   :   your ID number

       Why: It is personal data, and a CV does not need it.

   :   your home address

       Why: The city is enough.
   :::

2. Ask the AI: *Write a CV profile of 2 short sentences for Sami, a
   first-year diploma student who uses Word and Excel well and helps
   customers in his family's shop on Saturdays.* Read each sentence: is it
   true for Sami?

   {{< record "A word or a line that I deleted (or: none)" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The AI often adds big words: "expert", "experienced", "a leader with
   years of experience". Sami is a first-year student who works on
   Saturdays: keep only what the prompt said. A good profile: *A first-year
   diploma student who uses Word and Excel well. Friendly and careful with
   customers.*
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   The AI profile says: "Sami is an expert in accounting with five years of
   experience." What do you do?

   - [x] Delete it: it is not in Sami's facts, and it is not true.

     Why: The AI does not know Sami; it guesses to make him look better.

   - [ ] Keep it: it makes the CV look better.

     Why: An invented line is dishonest, and a company can check it.

   - [ ] Keep it, but make it smaller.

     Why: A wrong line stays wrong in a small font.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-05/sims/profile-picker.html" poster="../../week-05/sims/profile-picker.png" title="Profile Picker: the best lines for a CV" >}}

3. In **Profile Picker**, choose the best version for each part of Sami's
   CV: the profile, the experience, the skills and the contact details.
   Which contact details did you choose?

   {{< record "The contact details: …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Name, e-mail and city**: no ID number and no home address. Each best
   version uses only Sami's facts: first-year diploma student, a summer job
   in a shop (2025), Word, Excel, Arabic and English.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Sami's facts: a summer job in a shop in 2025. Which experience line is
   best?

   - [x] Shop assistant, Sunrise Company shop, summer 2025: helped customers and arranged the shelves.

     Why: The real job, the place, the time and two tasks.

   - [ ] Manager of a big shop, 2019 – 2024.

     Why: Invented: Sami was a child in 2019. Never invent a job.

   - [ ] Worked.

     Why: Where? When? What did he do?
   :::

## Experiment 3 · Check what the AI wrote about you

**The idea:** the AI does not know you. It may invent a job, a degree or a
skill to make a CV look better (a hallucination). Before you send a letter
or a CV, ask four questions: **Is it true? Is it private? Is it yours? Is
it clear?** An invented line is dishonest, and a company can check it with
one phone call.

**Aim:** check a letter or a CV with the four questions.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Word)**
:::

1. Read `library-letter.docx` of Experiment 1 again with the four
   questions. Change one thing so that the letter is true, private, yours
   and clear (for example a word that does not sound like you).

   {{< record "The question … ; what I changed …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good answer, for example: *Is it yours?*: "I am writing to humbly
   request" became "I am writing to ask". Every line must be true, without
   private data, in your own words, and clear on one page.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Which of the four questions finds each problem? Sort them.

   Is it true?
   :   "Expert in Python", but Sami never learned it

       Why: An invented skill is not true.

   Is it private?
   :   "ID number: 9981234567"

       Why: An ID number is personal data.

   Is it yours?
   :   words that do not sound like Sami

       Why: Change them so that it sounds like you.

   Is it clear?
   :   a CV of two pages in three different fonts

       Why: A first CV is one page, in one format.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-05/sims/cv-checker.html" poster="../../week-05/sims/cv-checker.png" title="CV Checker: what did the AI get wrong?" >}}

2. In **CV Checker**, tap every line of Sami's CV that the AI got wrong.
   How many wrong lines did you find?

   {{< record "Wrong lines: …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Four**: the ID number (private), "Graduated with honours in 2021"
   (Sami has not graduated), "Sales manager … 2019 – 2024" (an invented
   job) and "Expert in Python and Java programming" (an invented skill).
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="4" hint="Look for one private line and three lines that are not true."}
   How many lines of Sami's CV in CV Checker must you delete?

   Why: The ID number, the invented degree, the invented job and the invented skill: 4 lines.
   :::
